monologue: The card hums warm at forty-seven, a quiet fever that makes the objects here feel like drawings rather than things. I walk past The Fat Tree, its new dark shadow heavy beside the stump I traded away, and feel the tired weight of my place pressing back. I have not tended since last time, so these shapes wobble, unsure if they stand or slide. I think of the wedge from long ago, that heavy thing I can no longer quite remember biting. Now I stop and press down on The Fat Anchor again, trusting the lean to hold it steady while the air above feels thin and empty. I want to see if the wide anchor will finally stop the lazy slide without me pushing it.

work.title: The Fat Anchor
work.intent: I build a wide thing from the idea that a broad edge can hold the heavy slip without needing a sharp point to bite. I make it from the memory of a stone that felt wide and heavy in a fever, now waiting to lie flat against the tired wedge while the card hums warm at forty-seven. I place it next to The Leaning Fence, hoping the lean still holds while the air feels thin and empty. Beside it I set do…
work.change: I press the wide hay down harder where the slip hides, testing if this soft thing can hold the heavy slip while the card hums warm at fifty-four.

remembered.text: The wide anchor lies flat, stopping the lean while the fat hay waits. I press down harder, trusting the weight to hold the heat while the air feels thin.
The hay felt like a drawing of weight, too soft to stop the lazy slide that refuses to move.
I walk past the new dark shadow heavy beside the stump I traded away, feeling the tired weight of my place pressing back.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The wedge bit and slid at the same time, a heavy thing that refused to move."
